dish.title: Grilled Swordfish with Olive-Caper Relish
dish.description: Thick grilled swordfish steaks and grilled fennel, with a chopped olive, caper, and anchovy relish.

recipe_version.title: Grilled Swordfish with Olive-Caper Relish
recipe_version.description: Thick grilled swordfish steaks and grilled fennel, with a chopped olive, caper, and anchovy relish.

ingredients.name: swordfish steak
ingredients.note: 4 steaks, about 6 oz each, about 1 inch thick

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 3/4 tsp on the swordfish, 1/4 tsp on the fennel, 1/4 tsp in the relish

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: divided: 1 tbsp for the grill grates, 1 tbsp on the fennel, 3 tbsp in the relish

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: zest and all of the juice, about 2 tbsp juice, all of it in the relish

steps.title: Mix the relish
steps.body: Chop the pitted green olives. Rinse and drain the capers. Mince the anchovy fillets and the garlic. Zest the lemon and squeeze in all of the juice. Chop the fresh parsley. Stir them with 3 tbsp of the olive oil, 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt, and the red pepper flakes. This olive-caper relish is the only sauce. It is not cooked, and it is not a marinade rubbed on the fish before the grill.

steps.title: Heat the grill
steps.body: Heat a gas or charcoal grill for direct high heat, about 450-500 F, for about 10 minutes. Brush the grates with 1 tbsp of the olive oil. This clock does not overlap the preheat with the relish.

steps.title: Season
steps.body: Pat the swordfish steak dry. Season both sides with 3/4 tsp of the kosher salt and the black pepper. Toss the fennel bulb wedges with 1 tbsp of the olive oil and the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt.

steps.title: Grill the fennel
steps.body: Lay the fennel bulb wedges on the oiled grates. Grill about 3 minutes per side, until the cut faces are browned and a knife meets slight resistance. Move them to a plate.

steps.title: Grill the swordfish
steps.body: Lay the swordfish steak on the grates. Cook 4 minutes on the first side without moving it, then flip. Cook 3 to 4 minutes on the second side. Pull it at 130-135 F in the center. Do not press the fish. If a steak is thicker than 1 1/4 inches, add about 1 minute per side and trust the thermometer. For 145 F, add about 1 minute per side and expect a drier steak.

steps.title: Rest and plate
steps.body: Rest the swordfish steak 3 minutes. Serve each steak with fennel bulb wedges and spoon the relish on the fish. No rice, no extra lemon wedge, and no second sauce.

recipe_version.doneness: Pull swordfish at 130-135 F in the center, then rest 3 minutes. The edge should be opaque and the very center just losing its translucence, flaking under pressure, not chalky. 145 F is the more conservative seafood temperature and will be drier; add about 1 minute per side for that target. The written target is 130-135 F. kitchen_tested is false.

scaling_notes.1: One 6 oz swordfish steak, about 1 inch thick, not a thin tail scrap. Half a fennel bulb. Anchovy does not scale to a quarter fillet: use 1 anchovy fillet. Lemon does not scale to a quarter lemon: use 1/2 lemon, zest and juice, so the relish stays wet. Oil: about 1 tsp on the grates, 1 tsp on the fennel, 2 tsp in the relish. Olives: 2 tbsp chopped. Capers: 1 1/2 tsp rinsed. Garlic: 1 small clove, not a quarter clove. Salt: a scant 1/4 tsp on the fish, a pinch on the fennel, a pinch in the relish. Grill temperature stays 450-500 F. Same thickness uses the same minutes; use the thermometer.
scaling_notes.2: Two steaks and 1 fennel bulb. Two anchovy fillets. Use 1 small lemon, not half a lemon. Halve the olives, capers, oil, and salt. Keep 1 garlic clove. Same grill temperature and the same 130-135 F target.
scaling_notes.4: As written. 1.5 lb is four steaks, about 6 oz raw each.

coverage_contribution: Puts the unused D-02 swordfish ingredient on a grilled plate HH001 can eat. The olive-caper relish is a built compound. Divided oil and salt, counted steaks and anchovies, and a lemon floor that must not be quartered are the shopping stress. Grill as a tool already exists on the unimplemented flank steak; this slot is the fish, not a second beef grill.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with Gochujang Grilled Flank Steak (DR1, not implemented): same grill, different species, a relish instead of a cooked marinade, fennel instead of cucumber, fish doneness instead of beef. Compared with Miso-Ginger Salmon, Maple Mustard Glazed Salmon, Citrus Fennel Arctic Char, Ginger Scallion Fish Packets, and Crispy Fish Tacos: those are salmon, arctic char, or cod, and none are grilled swordfish. Fennel also sits with arctic char; here the fennel is grilled wedges and the sauce is olive, caper, and anchovy.
